subject: Post-demo: Crestview POC success criteria, owners & short timeline
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestview.ai>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@crestview.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Crestview POC success criteria, owners & short timeline

Hi Samir / Emily — thanks for a great demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum going. I pulled this together while it’s fresh; please flag anything I missed.

1) Objective (what success looks like)
- Validate that Redwood reduces median token latency for Crestview’s ingestion->response pipeline from ~450ms to <250ms at 2k concurrent sessions.
- Verify end-to-end integration for the search-to-generation flow against your 3 canonical prompts with no quality regressions (>90% pass per your rubric).
- Measure cost delta (tokens/server) and confirm model routing policy that keeps 95th latency under SLA.

2) Success criteria (owner / acceptance)
- Latency and throughput tests: Samir / Crestview infra team (accept if p50 <250ms, p95 <420ms with target load).
- Quality checks: Emily (accept if >=90% of curated prompts pass rubric).
- Integration & tracing: Ben (Redwood) will validate traces and KV cache effectiveness.

3) Proposed 2-week POC timeline (starts Mon 6/14)
- Week 0 (6/14): Access + baseline capture — Crestview provides sample workload, service account + VPC peering info. (Owner: Samir)
- Week 1 (6/14–6/20): Integration + perf tuning — Redwood config + routing policy applied. Run smoke tests. (Owners: Camila + Ben)
- Week 2 (6/21–6/27): Scale test & quality run — run canonical prompt set, gather metrics & artifacts, present findings. (Owners: Emily + Ben)

4) Immediate asks for Monday 6/14 kickoff
- Service account + API scoped keys (samir.patel@crestview.ai)
- Small sample dataset (5–10 representative conversations) uploaded to shared Drive link above
- Baseline metrics CSV (p50/p95 token latency, current concurrency settings)

5) Notes on deliverables
- Redwood will share a short success matrix (attached) and a config snippet (attached).
- We recommend a single canary model route for the first run to simplify comparisons.

Attachment: crestview-success-matrix.xlsx (overview), redwood-poc-config.yaml (example)

Next step: If you confirm owners + can provide the service account by EOD Monday (6/14), we’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for 6/14 10:00am PT to get the peering and keys sorted.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
(415) 555-0187

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestview.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@crestview.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Crestview POC success criteria, owners & short timeline

Thanks Camila — this is clean and actionable. A few quick items from our side:

- We can provide a service account and the sample dataset by EOD Monday (6/14). I’ll assign Ravi (infra) to work with your team on peering.
- One clarification on the latency target: p95 <420ms looks fine but can we include a note about acceptable degradation under cold-start conditions (first 30s of a burst)? We want to be explicit for the rubrics.
- For the rubric Emily will own, she asks whether Redwood can export per-prompt traces in CSV so she can tie quality checks to specific model responses.

Also — what’s the minimum concurrent session load you recommend for the 2k concurrent sessions test? We want to ensure we simulate real user behavior.

Samir
VP of Engineering | Crestview AI
samir.patel@crestview.ai

On Thu, Jun 10, 2027 at 3:12 PM Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message]

Date: 2027-06-11T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Crestview POC success criteria, owners & short timeline

Great points — responding inline:

- Cold-starts: Agreed. We’ll include an explicit cold-start window in the success matrix: max allowed degradation = +30% p95 for the first 30s after idle periods. I’ve updated the attached matrix. (Attachment: crestview-success-matrix.xlsx)
- Per-prompt traces: Yes, we can export per-request traces to CSV including request id, model route, kv-cache-hit, latency_ms, and response quality tag. We’ll include the CSV export in the final artifacts.
- Load profile: For the 2k concurrent sessions test we recommend a ramp from 200 -> 2k over 6 minutes with realistic think-times (modeled from your baseline file). If you prefer, we can run a steady-state run at 2k for 10 minutes after ramp to capture sustained behavior.

I will:
- Kick off the Drive folder and upload the two attachments again (crestview-success-matrix.xlsx, redwood-poc-config.yaml).
- Schedule the 30-min kickoff Monday 6/14 at 10:00am PT. Calendar invite to follow.

Marissa will own the contact list for the Crestview engineers and the calendar invite. Ben will be point for tracing and any config questions during the integration.

Camila

(Attachment: crestview-success-matrix.xlsx)

Samir / team — quick operational notes from the Redwood infra side:

- We’ll prepare the per-request CSV exports and a short script to tag kv-cache hits. I’ll drop the script into the Drive folder by Sunday.
- Regarding the test load — the ramp profile Camila suggested is sensible. We recommend running the steady-state 2k run in at least two separate 10-minute windows to catch variability.
- On credits: I’ve approved a $4k trial credit to cover peak GPU time for the POC. Camila — please confirm and I’ll route to finance for booking.

Ben Carter

ben@redwood.com

Subject: Monday kickoff + quick checklist / 48h nudge

Morning — quick nudge ahead of today’s 10:00am PT kickoff. We want to ensure the following are done so the session focuses on integration rather than access troubleshooting: 

- Samir: Service account + API key uploaded to Drive (or invite to your IAM test user). Please confirm the key name.
- Samir / Ravi: VPC peering details and CIDR ranges in the shared doc.
- Emily: Canonical prompt set uploaded (5–10 prompts) and the rubric sheet populated for QA.
- Marissa (Redwood): calendar invite sent; waiting on your attendance confirmations.

If any of these slip, propose we push the kickoff by 24 hours rather than waste time. Otherwise we’ll meet at 10:00am PT and run through peering, baseline capture, and a short smoke test.

Thanks — see you on the call.

Camila Reyes
